newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Kabila arrives for first OAU summit.
newsitem.headline: Kabila arrives for first OAU summit.

text.p: Newly installed Democratic Republic of Congo leader Laurent Kabila flew into Zimbabwe late Sunday to attend his first Organisation of African Unity summit.

Kabila, sporting a trademark safari suit and on his first trip outside Congo as president two weeks after chasing long-time ruler Mobutu Sese Seko from power, arrived aboard Mobutu's former presidential jet.

He was met at the airport by Zimbabwe President Robert Mugabe, whose government was reported to have supported Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo with arms and uniforms.
Kabila, sworn in as president four days ago, is on Monday scheduled to meet United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan, who arrived in the Zimbabwean capital earlier.

There were no details of the planned subject of their talks but on Saturday Kabila's government's denounced as intimidating and defamatory U.N. Security Council accusations that his army had massacred Hutu refugees on its soil.
The OAU summit, the first in Southern Africa for 25 years, is expected to discuss the Great Lakes crisis where military-ruled Burundi and Rwanda, two Kabila allies, are battling Hutu rebels.
